prompt: Build the Mount Rushmore of interstate highways. Numbers only, then defend one of them with your whole chest.
response:
10, 80, 90, 95

**In defense of 90:**

I-90 is the undisputed king of the American road, and I will not hear a single word to the contrary. Spanning a mind-boggling 3,021 miles, it is the longest interstate in the country, stitching together the very fabric of the United States from the Puget Sound in Seattle to the Massachusetts Bay in Boston. It doesn’t just cross the country; it *is* the country. 

You want scenery? I-90 gives you the majestic evergreen peaks of the Cascades, the rugged, alien beauty of the South Dakota Badlands (and literally drives you right past the actual Mount Rushmore), the sprawling Great Plains, and the dense, historic forests of New England. You want engineering marvels? It features the Homer M. Hadley Memorial Bridge in Washington, one of the longest floating bridges on earth. You want economic muscle? It barrels straight through the heart of Chicago, linking the agricultural behemoths of the Midwest with the ports of the East and West. 

It runs along the shores of the Great Lakes and traces the paths of pioneers. While other highways get bogged down in endless urban sprawl or boast just one type of climate, I-90 is a masterclass in American diversity—geographically, economically, and culturally. It is the ultimate American road trip, the absolute backbone of the northern United States, and the crown jewel of the Eisenhower Interstate System.
